bug_semantics: The authenticated POST /contact/save path trusted the request's numeric contact id and loaded Contact::find(...) without company_id scoping before overwriting the record, so a user could blindly modify another tenant's contact. The authenticated GET /contact/export-vcard/{id} path likewise used Contact::findOrFail($id) without company_id scoping and returned the selected record's vCard, allowing cross-tenant PII disclosure by id enumeration.
flaw_origin: The write primitive originated in 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9, which added the authenticated /contact/save route and a new ContactSaveController whose update branch selected a Contact solely by attacker-controlled id; contacts were already owned through company-scoped leads, so the missing ownership check was exploitable at introduction. Commit 9fda3ee70b7b6035f729a154f7bf50bfabbd3b7f later added an explicit contact.company_id on creation while retaining the unscoped update. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved the same vulnerable save logic into ContactRepository and is not the BIC. The independent vCard disclosure surface was added from scratch by a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9 shows author Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, a plain one-line message, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity
evidence: The first-party CNA record at https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-19433-idor-in-prospero-flow-crm-contact-save-and-vcard-export identifies ContactRepository::save and ContactExportVCard::export, the POST /contact/save and GET /contact/export-vcard/{id} attack paths, affected versions before 5.4.8, and direct patch f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398; it explicitly says the supplier equivalents changed by the patch were outside the proof of concept.

At vulnerable parent f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932, routes/module/contact.php exposes both routes; both controllers extend MainController, whose middleware is auth and locked. app/Repositories/ContactRepository.php uses Contact::find($data['id']) and then writes names, phones, email, job title, social profiles, and notes, while app/Http/Controllers/Contact/ContactExportVCard.php uses Contact::findOrFail($id) and downloads vCard content. Neither query constrains company_id. The sibling ContactUpdateController and ContactDeleteController do constrain id with Auth::user()->company_id, confirming the missing ownership predicate.

git log -L and git log -S traced the save lookup backward through app/Repositories/ContactRepository.php: 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d created the repository during a deduplication refactor but simultaneously removed the identical Contact::find($request->id) update branch from ContactSaveController. Continuing -L/-S on that controller reaches 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9, which added the controller and /contact/save route from scratch; thus 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d is a move, not the real BIC.

Direct parent-tree verification: git diff --name-status f84405497c20f4744b3ce55c847a122d9a77326d 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9 reports A app/Http/Controllers/Contact/ContactSaveController.php, and git ls-tree of f84405497c20f4744b3ce55c847a122d9a77326d at that path is empty. The BIC diff also adds the /contact/save route, so both the vulnerable handler and its exposure are absent from the immediate parent.

The disclosure primitive has its own smallest BIC: git log -L on app/Http/Controllers/Contact/ContactExportVCard.php reaches a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830, which creates the controller with Contact::findOrFail($id) and adds the GET route. Its parent c679dd4c6c19f9af636a61efc9408c18a4ad4239 has no such file (git ls-tree empty; name-status A). Its commit object is also solely human-authored and human-committed by Gustavo Novaro with no trailers.

git show f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398 directly replaces both unscoped contact lookups with id plus Auth::user()->company_id predicates and firstOrFail, and adds cross-tenant save/export regression tests. The same direct commit also hardens analogous supplier surfaces, but those are not needed to establish this advisory's fix.

Version/tag cross-check: git tag --contains shows both 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9 and a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830 are ancestors of v1.0.0 (and the later vulnerable tags v2.0.1 and v4.6.0). version.php is 5.4.7 at fix parent f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932 and remains 5.4.7 in the fix commit; the descendant 361566c1ddb01df16f2cff0aa836f04be174f3c4 bumps APP_VERSION to 5.4.8. The earliest tag containing f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398 is v5.5.3, whose version.php is 5.5.3. This matches the affected-before-5.4.8 boundary despite there being no v5.4.8 tag.

BIC-only AI check: raw commit object 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9 has one parent, human author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, and no AI/bot trailer or identity. The Claude co-author trailer on the 2026 fix f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398 is later fix-only evidence and is excluded from BIC attribution.
reasoning: This advisory combines two independently introduced IDOR sinks. The lifecycle begins with the blind-write sink in 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9: an authenticated numeric-id update endpoint was created without checking that the target contact belonged to the caller's company. Tenant ownership already existed via the contact's company-scoped lead relationship; explicit contact.company_id was added later without repairing the lookup. The vulnerable lookup survived formatting and feature edits, then moved unchanged into ContactRepository in 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d. The vCard read sink was independently created in a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830 and survived until the same fix. Immediate-parent trees prove the selected earliest BIC's handler and route did not exist before it, and separately prove the export primitive's absence before its own BIC. Both primitives shipped in tagged releases. Commit f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398 directly closes both by adding authenticated company_id predicates; the next descendant version bump establishes 5.4.8 as the patched boundary. Because the smallest selected BIC's raw commit object has no AI marker and is wholly human-authored/committed, later Claude attribution on the fix cannot causally attribute the introduction, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
